method: 400 authored situations x 5 workflow branches = 2,000 design scenarios. Source links support the research context. Individual scenarios are original synthetic requirements, not reported incidents, legal determinations, or 2,000 executed tests. A mapped code path establishes an existing subsystem, not coverage of every scenario assigned to it.

sources.name: TREC wholesaling survey
sources.note: Survey responses identify confusion over the wholesaler role, unexpected costs, failed end-buyer placement and title-office reluctance. This is qualitative context, not a current failure rate for iCash.

sources.name: HomeVestors seller concerns
sources.note: A cash-buying operator describes seller concerns about identity, hidden fees and buyers backing out. Its marketing claims and business-specific promises are not adopted as iCash terms.

sources.name: TREC written-disclosure update
sources.note: Texas requires written disclosure of the wholesaler’s interest to buyers and sellers. Transaction templates and advertising must reflect the actual role.

sources.name: American Bar Association purchase-contract guide
sources.note: Price, possession, contingencies, acceptance and deadlines belong to the agreement. The scenario design treats amendments and signatures as distinct from conversational intent.

sources.name: Texas Department of Insurance title FAQ
sources.note: The state regulator distinguishes a conditional title commitment from a policy and lists ownership, authority, recording and lien defects. The scenarios turn these issue classes into evidence-gathering and professional-resolution tasks.

sources.name: ALTA wire-fraud resources
sources.note: Changing payment instructions and seller impersonation require independent verification. The AI can coordinate verification without becoming the custodian or sender of closing funds.

sources.name: Oregon Real Estate Agency wholesaling requirements
sources.note: Oregon has registration or licensing and written-disclosure requirements. A nationwide workflow cannot apply one state’s authorization everywhere.

sources.name: CFPB closing process
sources.note: Closing coordination, execution, funding and ownership transfer are different events. Mortgage-specific disclosures are not imposed on every cash assignment by this report.

gaps.title: Seller intent must survive channel changes
gaps.current: Direct-response refusal rules, seller evidence and callback logic exist. Every new source still needs the correct delivered-question and role context.
gaps.gap: Cross-channel refusals, ownership denials and future-contact preferences require scenario-level verification; this audit does not claim every variant is already handled.
gaps.fix: Use one source-bound intent record for seller texts and completed calls. Cancel unsent contradictory work; distinguish no-to-owner, no-to-sale and text-only.

gaps.title: Resolve ordinary multi-intent replies
gaps.current: Seller dialogue and numeric offer execution can ask missing questions and explain assignment. The text analysis schema still has a broad review action.
gaps.gap: One message can combine price, timing, repairs and a question. A single review classification can strand otherwise answerable parts.
gaps.fix: Persist all supported intents, answer the factual parts, and ask one missing question. Store unresolved parts as typed dependencies rather than stopping the whole deal.

gaps.title: Keep offers evidence-based and versioned
gaps.current: Seller high asks can receive supported automatic counteroffers. Acceptance is bound to actual delivered terms; new offers use the current formula.
gaps.gap: New condition, payoff and net-price facts must invalidate only affected proposed terms. Already signed terms cannot silently change.
gaps.fix: Re-underwrite from verified new facts, save the new version and request its exact acceptance. Ask for missing inputs automatically.
gaps.status: Existing mechanisms; expanded acceptance scenarios specified

gaps.title: Inspection work needs its own executable tasks
gaps.current: Condition questions, repair estimates, viewing coordination and generic closing tasks exist.
gaps.gap: The inspected paths do not establish a complete inspector booking, utility/access, report collection and renegotiation workflow.
gaps.fix: Add source-bound inspection tasks with access scope, responsible payer, appointment, report and contractual deadline. A new report triggers prospective underwriting and the required party decision.

gaps.title: Buyer calls can record requests without executing them
gaps.current: Buyer voice policies explicitly record requests for review and cannot claim package, agreement or title delivery. Buyer SMS has a separate executable journey.
gaps.gap: A useful buyer call can end without a source-bound job for its supported request.
gaps.fix: Build a post-call action adapter for exact completed buyer-call evidence. Map package, signer-details and viewing requests to existing handlers, retaining duplicate protection and real authority. Buyer outbound remains SMS/email.

gaps.title: Contract recovery must retain the original envelope
gaps.current: Signing validates exact terms, required signers and original provider operations. Customer signatures and legal changes remain distinct actions.
gaps.gap: Missing details, access problems and uncertain provider outcomes need precise recovery paths; removing every signing hold would create duplicate or unauthorized agreements.
gaps.fix: Automate missing-field collection and original receipt reconciliation. Present only the real signature or specific terms decision to the authorized party.

gaps.title: Deadlines need a specific recovery owner
gaps.current: Closing tasks and journey retry times exist. The supervisor stores a next check, but some next steps remain broad review text.
gaps.gap: A check timestamp alone does not execute a missing inspection, extension, payoff or notice workflow.
gaps.fix: Attach the signed deadline, responsible party, required evidence and permitted reminder to each dependency. Escalate the specific unresolved decision before expiry; never extend a signed deadline automatically.

gaps.title: Title intake and curative work remain partly manual
gaps.current: Title search, qualification, document handoff, messages, follow-ups and tasks exist. Automatic status confirmation expects a rigid six-line message.
gaps.gap: Ordinary closer emails can produce suggestions or review instead of executable requests for missing documents. Legal cures are not completed by a generic status change.
gaps.fix: Extract nonbinding document requests from verified current replies into tasks. Request missing fields automatically; use authoritative confirmation for milestones and assign specific curative work to the closer.

gaps.title: Showings need accurate active-step display
gaps.current: Seller availability and separate buyer/seller confirmations exist. Access requests can resolve automatically when a buyer chooses an available time.
gaps.gap: The UI inactivity fallback could override a proposed or confirmed visit. A fallback also claimed viewing options existed when the buyer had not requested a visit.
gaps.fix: Preserve actual visit progress ahead of generic inactivity review and show a neutral buyer-choice step when no visit is requested. Further access/rescheduling cases remain acceptance requirements.
gaps.status: Focused UI behavior fix implemented and tested locally

gaps.title: Buyer search must prove usable demand
gaps.current: Discovery, enrollment, contact metadata and ranking exist. Preferences are not verified funds or successful closing capacity.
gaps.gap: No blanket proof exists that each property obtains a qualified buyer within its contractual deadline.
gaps.fix: Track eligible reach, replies, verified readiness and time-to-deposit. Widen only approved search tiers and retain backup candidates without promising competing reservations.

gaps.title: Compound package requests fell through to review
gaps.current: The live pure classifier returned null for “Send photos and property details” while recognizing “Send me details”. The same authorized package satisfies both nouns.
gaps.gap: A harmless conjunction prevented an existing automatic answer.
gaps.fix: Recognize an entire request containing only two to five package-information items. Reuse the current source-bound package reply. Mixed wire, refund, signing, access or conditional requests remain outside this narrow parser.
gaps.status: Focused SQL fix implemented and tested locally

gaps.title: Buyer exception resolution needs delegated limits
gaps.current: The private buyer page records access, timing, price, repairs, funding and human blockers. Non-access resolution generally requires a versioned owner outcome.
gaps.gap: Routine questions can become manual work; changed commercial terms lack a complete bounded automatic negotiation policy.
gaps.fix: Separate factual questions from actual term changes. Answer facts automatically. Define explicit price, fee, date and deposit bounds before enabling automatic counteroffers or buyer replacement; preserve signed terms and actual human requests.

gaps.title: Payment claims are not verified money
gaps.current: Deposit, title-reported disbursement and owner-confirmed proceeds are separate. Ordinary title replies only create suggestions; certain contractions were not excluded by the suggestion parser.
gaps.gap: Fully automatic money receipt needs authoritative escrow/bank evidence. “The deposit wasn’t received” could incorrectly produce a positive suggestion, although it did not automatically settle funds.
gaps.fix: Reject negated title suggestions. Add verified receipt integrations and exact amount/file/payee matching before automating receipt confirmation. Keep wire changes and disputes in the authorized verification process.
gaps.status: Negation fix implemented locally; receipt integration remains

gaps.title: Jurisdiction coverage cannot be assumed
gaps.current: Signing policy and transaction authority checks exist. This audit has not verified an exhaustive current state-by-state rules catalog.
gaps.gap: Texas disclosure and Oregon registration illustrate materially different prerequisites.
gaps.fix: Maintain versioned jurisdiction requirements with approved templates, effective dates and required professionals. Automate document gathering; block only the unsupported regulated step until its prerequisite is satisfied.

gaps.title: Supervision must lead to an executable next step
gaps.current: The enabled supervisor can restore an absent seller reply job, enqueue missing fulfillment and advance an existing journey. It retains original uncertain operations and isolates deal failures.
gaps.gap: Many blocked reasons still describe what to review rather than invoking a handler to obtain the missing item. The current supervisor does not establish 2,000-case coverage.
gaps.fix: Extend existing supervision with typed dependency resolvers, deadline-aware queues and once-only action receipts. Do not replace the existing engine or clear unknown actions to manufacture progress.
gaps.status: Enabled narrow foundation; broader handlers needed

gaps.title: The existing UI must tell the truth about progress
gaps.current: Property cards, messages, signing, buyer coordination and closing panels already display next actions.
gaps.gap: Some presentation falls back to generic user review. A new internal recovery task must not appear as a completed call, contract, showing or payment.
gaps.fix: Use existing surfaces to display actual status, the missing item and the next step. Keep technical faults in private diagnostics. This release corrects two journey-state display errors without a layout change.
gaps.status: Focused display fixes implemented; broader mapping specified
